neighbours.label: the token inside a fixed idiom or formulaic phrase just before its completion (par for the course, crane his neck, his merry way, Row, row), versus the same words in literal, open phrasing
fire: Missing the bus on a Monday is about par for the course in this town.
The children had to crane their necks to see the parade over the adults.
After paying the bill, the travelers went on their merry way.
She sat on the bench, crossing her arms and frowning at the rain.
The kids chanted Twinkle, twinkle, little star until bedtime.
He shrugged his shoulders and said nothing more about it.
The old woman wagged her finger at the boys stealing apples.
Every winter, my uncle reads The Rime of the Ancient Mariner aloud.
quiet: Missing the bus on a Monday means a long walk to school in this town.
The children had to stand on chairs to see the parade over the adults.
After paying the bill, the travelers waited outside for a taxi.
She sat on the bench, reading a book and drinking her tea.
The kids sang several songs together until bedtime.
He packed his bags and said nothing more about it.
The old woman shouted at the boys stealing apples.
Every winter, my uncle reads a long novel aloud by the fire.
